subject: Establishment of a Municipal Affordable Housing Trust
overview: The Council discussed the creation of an affordable housing trust and a PILOT commission to manage non-profit contributions. It also addressed neighborhood concerns regarding traffic safety, gas leaks, and unregulated donation bins.

items.title: Ceremonial items and withdrawals
items.summary: The council tabled a citation for Max Stephens and noted the withdrawal of item 20-018.

items.title: Gas leak five-year plan
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting that the city administration work with National Grid to establish a five-year plan for repairing level 2 and level 3 gas leaks. The council cited safety, quality of life, and climate change as primary reasons for the request.

items.title: Food truck ordinance
items.summary: Approved a resolution to move forward with a food truck ordinance to replace the current case-by-case licensing process.

items.title: PILOT commission framework
items.summary: Approved a request for the city solicitor to provide a framework for a Payments in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) commission to negotiate community benefits and cash payments with non-profits like Tufts University. Councilors discussed the need for public input and clearer definitions of community benefits.

items.title: Short-term rental regulations
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting a draft ordinance to regulate short-term rentals, including a public registry and safety inspections. The matter was amended to include previously discussed papers on the topic.

items.title: Donation bin regulation
items.summary: Approved a resolution for the health and building departments to investigate furniture and clothing donation bins at the Fellsway Shopping Area and Mystic Avenue. The council amended the motion to issue a cease-and-desist order if the building department does not provide a formal response.

items.title: Main Street message board and Fellsway lighting
items.summary: Placed on file a report that the Main Street message board has been removed and approved a request for the state to improve lighting at the Fellsway and Bradbury Street intersection.

items.title: Health impacts of flashing crosswalk beacons
items.summary: Referred a petition regarding the health effects of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons to the city engineer to check for federal compliance and adjust flash rates. Residents testified that the strobe-like lights can trigger migraines and seizures.

items.title: Golden Avenue resurfacing
items.summary: Approved a request for a cost estimate and a Request for Proposals to resurface Golden Avenue due to the failure of temporary patching.

items.title: LoConte Rink Zamboni replacement
items.summary: Approved a resolution to replace the Zamboni at LoConte Rink and retain the current machine as a spare. The council amended the motion to request a professional assessment of the current machine's remaining lifespan.

items.title: South Street traffic calming
items.summary: Approved a request for the Chief of Police and the administration to provide updates on previously voted traffic calming measures for South Street, including stop signs and trucking route changes. Councilors expressed frustration over the lack of local action following extensive public hearings on the matter.

items.title: Municipal Affordable Housing Trust
items.summary: Referred to the Committee of the Whole a proposal to establish a Municipal Affordable Housing Trust to support low-to-moderate income households. Discussion focused on potential funding sources and whether developers should be allowed to pay fees in lieu of building units on-site.

items.title: Routine business
items.summary: Approved a committee report on marijuana ordinances, a moment of silence for firefighter Robert Minichiello, and the meeting minutes from January 7.
